sentences.text: This extinct bird possessed a skull with a concave parietal wall and bones in its chest that had not yet fused together.
Its feet looked like those of owls, including a fourth toe that could turn backward.
Fossils of this genus were discovered in the Middle Miocene Monkey Beds of La Venta, Colombia.
Evidence suggests its arms had special adaptations for hooking onto tree branches, a trait necessary for a bird with low mobility living in a jungle.
The genus was first described by Miller in 1953.
Only one species, Hoazinoides magdalenae, is known from this group.
Hoazinoides belongs to the order Cuculiformes, which contains modern cuckoos and hoatzins.
Tab Rasmussen established the family Hoazinoididae in 1997 because of the genus's unique skeletal features.
However, some experts argue it should not be placed in the hoatzin family, leaving its exact relationship to modern hoatzins uncertain.
This animal lived in Colombia during the Middle Miocene, specifically the Laventan age.
The time range for Hoazinoides spans from 15.98 to 10 million years ago.
